react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct network, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant signal. In the RaMP ORA, the broad Reactome 'Metabolism' super-pathway (R-HSA-1430728) ranks first (FDR=0.00165, fold-enrichment=35.8) driven by L-cysteine, coumarin, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (3-HAA). The WikiPathways 'ADHD and autism (ASD) pathways' (WP:WP5420) is the highest-specificity hit (FDR=0.00165, fold-enrichment=165.3), also anchored by L-cysteine and 3-HAA. Separately, the Mummichog m/z network returns tyrosine metabolism as its top hit (p=0.00437, overlap=4/4 compounds), driven by 7,8-dihydrobiopterin and several coumarate derivatives. The same network identifies tryptophan metabolism (p=0.0108) and biopterin metabolism (p=0.0108) as rank-1 and rank-2 network modules. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers thiamine metabolism (hsa00730, p=0.0131) and glutathione metabolism (hsa00480, p=0.0150) as KEGG-namespace hits, both anchored on L-cysteine. Cross-paradigm verification via HUMAN1:tryptophan_metabolism and HUMAN1:glutathione_metabolism confirms that 3-HAA (CHEBI:15793) and L-cysteine (CHEBI:17561) are bonafide roster members of those pathways. The two unresolved compounds (N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, methimazole) and bromide could not be canonicalised and do not appear in any enrichment hit set — they likely represent annotation noise or are truly orphan metabolites in the reference DBs. The convergent biological story is that treatment induces a coordinated perturbation of aromatic amino acid catabolism (tryptophan → 3-HAA) intersecting with folate/biopterin cofactor metabolism and the glutathione-dependent oxidative stress response, all centring on L-cysteine as a hub sulfur donor. Coumarin as a cytochrome P450 substrate in Biological Oxidations (R-HSA-211859, FDR=0.00165) suggests Phase-I xenobiotic metabolism is co-activated. The biopterin-axis is the strongest cross-paradigm bridge, appearing in both the m/z network (dihydrobiopterin as a network node) and the KEGG PSEA (thiamine/biosynthesis proximity).

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment paradigms reveal treatment-induced perturbations in oxidative metabolism and aromatic amino acid catabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=0.00165) and Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (REACT:R-HSA-71291, FDR=0.00165) as top Reactome hits, with L-cysteine and coumarin driving the Biological oxidations signal. The same ORA identifies ADHD and autism (ASD) pathways (WP:WP5420, FDR=0.00165, fold-enrichment=165.26) as the highest-specificity WikiPathways hit, anchored by L-cysteine and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently recovers Tyrosine metabolism (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism, p=0.0032) as the top-ranked pathway with 4 overlapping compounds, followed by Biopterin metabolism (MUMM:biopterin_metabolism, p=0.0106) and Tryptophan metabolism (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism, p=0.0106). The convergence of Mummichog's tryptophan and biopterin axis with RaMP's amino-acid oxidation pathway suggests that dihydrobiopterin and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid form a cross-paradigm bridge connecting tetrahydrobiopterin regeneration to tryptophan-derived niacin precursor flux. L-cysteine is the most-connected node, appearing in four of the ten RaMP pathways and linking oxidative stress defense to sulfur metabolism.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment paradigms reveal treatment-induced perturbations in oxidative metabolism and aromatic amino acid catabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=0.00165) and Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (REACT:R-HSA-71291, FDR=0.00165) as top Reactome hits, with L-cysteine and coumarin driving the Biological oxidations signal. The same ORA identifies ADHD and autism (ASD) pathways (WP:WP5420, FDR=0.00165, fold-enrichment=165.26) as the highest-specificity WikiPathways hit, anchored by L-cysteine and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently recovers Tyrosine metabolism (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism, p=0.0032) as the top-ranked pathway with 4 overlapping compounds, followed by Biopterin metabolism (MUMM:biopterin_metabolism, p=0.0106) and Tryptophan metabolism (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism, p=0.0106). The convergence of Mummichog's tryptophan and biopterin axis with RaMP's amino-acid oxidation pathway suggests that dihydrobiopterin and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid form a cross-paradigm bridge connecting tetrahydrobiopterin regeneration to tryptophan-derived niacin precursor flux. L-cysteine is the most-connected node, appearing in four of the ten RaMP pathways and linking oxidative stress defense to sulfur metabolism.
